title: source.rank result data
description: Evidence sources for one account ordered by the recency of their data. This is a recency ordering only; it carries no judgement of source reliability, authority or quality. It contains IDs, timestamps and counts, never record content.

ranking_basis.description: Fixed marker: sources are ordered by data recency alone, never by reliability, authority or quality.

timestamp_precedence.description: Field precedence applied per item, highest first. retrieved_at is a source-level fallback used only when no item of the source has a usable published_at or occurred_at.

sources.description: Data-dated sources first, then retrieval-fallback sources (each group by latest timestamp descending, ties by source_id ascending), then recency-unknown sources by source_id ascending.

rank.description: 1-based position among dated sources; null when recency is unknown. Tied sources still receive distinct ranks (see tied_with).

source_id_basis.description: Which field identified the source. source_type is the coarse fallback used when no provider is available.

recency.description: dated: ranked by a published_at/occurred_at data timestamp; retrieval_fallback: only retrieved_at was available (an upper bound on data age, not data recency); unknown: no usable timestamp.

age_days.description: Whole days from latest_data_at to now. Negative when the timestamp is later than now.

record_count.description: Accepted items (records plus evidence items) attributed to this source.

supporting_record_ids.description: Source record IDs whose timestamp equals latest_data_at.

supporting_evidence_ids.description: Evidence IDs whose timestamp equals latest_data_at.

tied_with.description: Other source_ids with the same latest_data_at and recency class. Order between tied sources is source_id ascending.

invalid_timestamp_count.description: Timestamp values present on this source's items that were unparseable and treated as missing.
